transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I came in because... I guess nothing really feels like mine anymore. I used to get excited about things, you know? Going for runs, watching basketball, checking out murals... even just making a really good drink at work. But lately... I don't know. I just stand there. It's like I just don't care about any of it at all.
How long have you been feeling this way—when did you first notice you stopped caring about things you used to enjoy?

It's been about two months now. It started right around the time the bar I work at got bought out. Everything I had been working toward there just... got changed. Since then, I just haven't cared about much.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep—trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual—since this started?

Yeah, my sleep's been pretty bad. I'll get into bed, and I'm tired, you know? But my brain just won't shut off. I just lie there, going over every little mistake I made at work that night. And then, when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I end up waking up at like four or five in the morning. Once I'm awake then, that's it. I can't get back to sleep at all.
Have you been feeling unusually worthless, guilty, or like you're a burden or failure, since this all started?

Yeah, I have. I just... I keep thinking about how I let down the younger bartenders at the place. And these local artists, too—I had promised them some space to put up their work before the buyout happened. Now that's all gone. I just feel like I completely wrecked their shot, you know? It really weighs on me. Honestly, I feel like I deserve whatever happens to me now for messing that up for them.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks or more of feeling this down, losing interest, or having similar symptoms—at any earlier point in your life?

No, I haven't. I mean, I've had bad days or, you know, tough weeks before—everyone does. But nothing like this. I've never felt this down for months at a time, or just... stopped caring about things. This is the first time anything like this has happened to me.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that you'd be better off dead since this started?
No, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean, I feel pretty miserable, like I said, but... no, I don't think I'd be better off dead. I would never actually hurt myself.

How has this been affecting your ability to actually get through your workday or handle your daily responsibilities—are you still able to function pretty normally, or has it become really difficult to keep up with things?

It's gotten pretty difficult, honestly. I've missed several shifts lately, which isn't like me. And when I am there, I've been making mistakes during closing... things I never used to mess up. Now my coworkers are having to double-check my work, and people used to just trust me to get it right. Outside of work, I've just stopped doing things. I used to go for runs, play basketball with some friends, or go shoot photos of murals around town... but I just can't bring myself to show up for any of that anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past two months?

Yeah, I've lost some weight. I just don't really have an appetite anymore. Most days, I honestly forget to eat until my hands start shaking while I'm working behind the bar. Even then, I might just grab a few bites of whatever's left in the kitchen after closing, usually something cold. And even that... I just feel sick looking at it. I force it down, but I don't want it.
Have you noticed your thinking or movements feeling noticeably slowed down, or trouble concentrating and making even simple decisions, since this started?

Yeah, my thinking has definitely been off. It's really hard to concentrate lately. Like, doing inventory used to be totally automatic for me. But now, I just stand there and stare at the bottles. I'll lose count three times just trying to get through one shelf. 

And making decisions... I actually freeze up trying to decide something really simple, like what garnish to restock first for the shift. It's like my brain just gets stuck and I can't figure out what to do next.

Would you say that despite all this difficulty, you're still managing to get through most of your day-to-day tasks and self-care, or has it reached the point where you're barely able to do even basic things like getting out of bed, showering, or feeding yourself?

I'm barely getting by, to be honest. I mean, I guess I'm still doing some things, but it's really hard. Getting out of bed takes a lot out of me. I'll just lie there for hours before I finally force myself up. And showering... I've been skipping that a lot more than I should. It just feels like too much effort. Like I said about eating, I'm just not doing it unless I absolutely have to. I wouldn't say I'm completely bedridden, but I'm definitely not taking care of myself the way I used to. It's just... everything feels like it takes so much energy, and I don't have any left.
